title: The Sticky Paint Surprise
markdown:
Iris and Button were super excited for painting day. They practically bounced into Professor Elm’s art room, ready to splish and splash.

The room was a sticky, slippery, splattery mess. Red, blue, yellow—like a rainbow had exploded and got super gooey. Brushes lay on their sides like tired fish. A yellow puddle had already found the cupboard door. Button’s paw went into bright red with a wet schlop. “Whoa!” Iris mumbled, pulling her sticky shoe free. “It’s like walking on bubblegum!” She tried to wipe a smear, but it just spread, getting bigger and bigger, a red map of a place nobody wanted to visit. This was not painting. It was sticky chaos.

Then Professor Elm arrived. “My, my,” he hooted. “What a mess!” He explained that tiny invisible things called germs love to hitch rides on sticky paint. “You can’t even see them,” he said, “but they hop onto your fingers, then your toys, spreading stickiness everywhere.” He dipped a wing in a small bowl of water. “But water,” he added, showing a tiny bottle of bubbly soap, “is like a super clean-up crew. It nudges those invisible hitchhikers right off.”

Iris’s eyes lit up. A puzzle. “So the water and soap wash the germs away?”

Button nodded. “And the sticky paint goes too?”

Professor Elm smiled. “Exactly. Iris, you guide the rags. Button, you nudge the sticky bits together. I’ll be the chief soaper.”

So they got to work with new excitement. Iris calmly showed them where to scrub, starting at the biggest puddle and working toward the door, the way you tidy a puzzle from the corners in. Button nudged the sticky puddles towards the rags, humming a small busy tune. Professor Elm added bubbly soap, and the paint washed away cleanly, colour sliding off the floor in cheerful ribbons. Soon the floor gleamed. The room smelled fresh, like a window had been opened on purpose, and Button’s red paw was only a paw again.

“Hooray!” cheered Button.

Iris beamed. “We solved it!”

Professor Elm smiled. “You did. Washing hands with soap and water sends germs down the drain. It keeps us healthy so we can paint more amazing pictures.” He winked. “Now, about that dragon and berry bush…”

Iris and Button’s eyes sparkled. “I wonder,” Iris mused, “what other hidden helpers are all around us?”

Professor Elm just smiled, because that was the best question of all—especially if the next helper came in a bottle and a bowl, and left enough clean floor for a dragon.
characters: Iris (puzzle solver), Button (sticky-pawed badger), Elm (art-room professor)
author: StoryGen Community
